# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft Against Our Playbook

I've reviewed the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter against our negotiation positions. Below are the material departures, my reasoning, and recommendations. Multiple seller positions are more aggressive than our baseline and several require pushback.

---

## 1. General Liability Cap — Clause 12.1 ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Our position:** Starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% / 4,800,000 cap is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from **Amelia Frost**, identifying the draft — **none has been given**.

**Push back:** Reject and revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. We are not authorised to accept 20% here. Do not let this be presented as "already agreed" — the Seller labels it a "negotiated position," but it is not one we've conceded. Flag internally: if anyone wants to accept 20%, they need Frost's written sign-off first.

---

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2 ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** De minimis **AUD 25,000**; basket **AUD 250,000**; only the **excess above** the basket recoverable (a true deductible/excess basket).
**Our position:** De minimis **AUD 5,000**; aggregate basket **AUD 50,000**; seller liable **from the first dollar** once exceeded (a tipping/first-dollar basket).

**Push back:** Three separate problems here — all adverse:
- De minimis is **5x** too high.
- Basket is **5x** too high.
- The "excess above the basket" mechanic is a deductible, not our first-dollar tipping basket. This is a structural change that further erodes recovery beyond the numbers.

Revert all three to playbook figures and restore first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded.

---

## 3. Time Limits — Clause 12.3/13 ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; and a sweeper that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise**."
**Our position:** **24 months** general period; 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval (**none given**).

**Push back:** Revert to 24 months. The "all Claims unless expressly stated" sweeper is a trap — it's designed to pull fundamental/title, tax and fraud into the short general limitation by default. Reject the sweeper and insist on **expressly separate regimes** (see next point).

---

## 4. Fundamental/Title Collapsed into General Regime ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** Capacity and title warranties to be subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Our position:** Fundamental/Title have a **separate regime** — 100% cap, at least **six years**, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

**Push back:** Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cut our fundamental protections by 80% on cap and to 18 months on time. These must be carved out and kept separate. This is one of the most damaging asks in the draft because it quietly guts title protection.

---

## 5. Limitations/Exclusive Remedy/Non-Reliance Apply to "All Claims" — 9.3/12.8/20.5 ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
**Our position:** **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**

**Push back:** Non-negotiable. Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that overrides every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision. Also ensure fundamental/title and specific indemnities are not swept in. Reject "all Claims of any nature" as drafted.

---

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2 ⚠️ High

**Seller:** General/deemed disclosure of the **entire data room** (DD-002 to DD-012) "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026," plus **Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records**.
**Our position:** Require **specific, fair disclosure**; **reject** whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search/deemed disclosure.

**Push back:** Reject blanket and deemed disclosure. Require that only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** (with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter) qualify. Delete the sweep-in of public registers and the whole data room. Note §1.4's non-admission wording is standard, but the general disclosure architecture itself is the problem.

---

## 7. Buyer Knowledge — Clause 8.3 ⚠️ Critical

**Seller:** Buyer has **no claim** for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records**.
**Our position:** **Delete** blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Push back:** This is an aggressive imputed/constructive-knowledge bar ("discoverable") layered on top of the deemed disclosure in #6 — together they would defeat most claims. Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named individuals and must expressly exclude title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

---

## 8. Bluefen Consent — Clause 3/6.3 & Disclosure §2 ⚠️ High

**Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours" and consent treated as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is **~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m)**.
**Our position:** Require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is **insufficient** for a material customer.

**Push back:** For a customer worth ~30% of revenue, reasonable endeavours and "consent on delivery" are inadequate. Make it a **Condition Precedent** that effective consent is obtained **and** its clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied/evidenced before Completion. Do not accept delivery of a bare consent document as sufficient.

---

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7 & Disclosure §3 ⚠️ High

**Seller:** Release to be provided **following Completion**; ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, **not repaid**, **no discharge of security** included.
**Our position:** Require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval**.

**Push back:** Reject post-completion release as the default. Require a current payout statement, **direct repayment out of completion funds**, and effective release/discharge of security at or before Completion. If any residual timing gap is unavoidable, we need an **irrevocable release undertaking from the bank** — and Frost's approval. On a debt-free/cash-free deal this AUD 3.2m must be cleared, not left floating.

---

## 10. Employee Bonuses — Funds Flow & Disclosure §5 ⚠️ High

**Seller:** DD-005 closing bonuses of **AUD 420,000** are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in the funds flow. Disclosure confirms they're **omitted** and is **silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs**.
**Our position:** The AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**; the funds flow must **not silently exclude** them.

**Push back:** This is a silent omission that shifts cost to us. Require the AUD 420,000 **and** the associated on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) to be either an explicit funds-flow line item or expressly seller-funded (e.g., via a specific indemnity / purchase-price adjustment). Do not accept "a matter for the Seller" while the economic burden sits with the company post-Completion.

---

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 & Disclosure §4 ⚠️ Medium

**Seller:** Indemnity **limited to the specific SOW3 payment**, said to be "adequate." DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but **not independently verified**, and **no receipt or confirmatory assignment** is in the data room.

**Our position:** **Broaden** the narrow indemnity while **preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified** either way.

**Push back:** The risk is broader than a single payment — if SOW3 fees aren't cleared, Project Materials/IP may not transfer, affecting ownership and use. Broaden the indemnity to cover the IP-transfer/assignment consequences, not just the payment, while preserving the ability to cure by payment. Don't concede the AUD 180,000 figure as settled — it's unverified.

---

## 12. Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006) — Clause 4.6/Schedule 6 & Disclosure §6 ⚠️ Medium

**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material." Disclosure: download link sent to an **unintended external address**, possibly **~1,240 records** (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); **does not establish** access, scope or notification duty; **no loss amount**.
**Our position:** **Preserve logs, investigate, require updates**; assume **NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** either way.

**Push back:** Don't accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation as a conclusion — but equally don't overstate it. Require covenants to **preserve all logs/evidence, continue investigating, and provide updates** through to Completion (and a reasonable tail). Consider a **specific indemnity** for defined incident costs if the investigation escalates. Keep our position neutral on whether a breach/notification duty exists.

---

## 13. Sandbar Supplier Renewals — Disclosure §8 ⚠️ Low/Medium

**Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (**AUD 330,000** aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure notes it does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in ordinary course, and flags they should be **read together** for timing/scope.
**Our position:** **Assess**; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction**.

**Push back:** Don't accept either characterisation reflexively. Diligence whether these are committed/accrued vs. terminable, and whether the "read together" timing suggests an attempt to structure around a threshold. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction, but reserve the point pending assessment.

---

## 14. Title — Clause/§10 & DD-012 ⚠️ High

**Seller:** Title "evidenced by the Company share register at **DD-012**." Disclosure §10 admits this is the **source relied on** and that the **Buyer has not completed its own verification**.
**Our position:** Require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**.

**Push back:** A self-produced share register is **not independent proof** of title. Require independent verification of ownership, encumbrances and the Seller's authority/capacity (e.g., ASIC searches, corporate authorisations, confirmation of no security interests over the shares — PPSR). Tie this to the fundamental/title regime in #4.

---

## 15. Tax / IP Warranties — "Settled under the General Regime" ⚠️ Medium

**Seller:** Treats tax and IP warranty positions as **settled under the general regime** (i.e., caught by the 20% cap / 18 months / basket above).
**Our position:** Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume **no unlimited liability and no resolution**. Keep Tax/IP categories **separate** with no hidden general-regime override.

**Push back:** Reject the premise that these are "settled." They are open. Resist folding tax (which typically warrants a longer period aligned to statutory assessment periods) and IP into the general cap/time regime by default. Keep them as separate, still-to-be-negotiated categories.

---

## 16. Office Lease / Mossvale — Disclosure §§7, 9 ℹ️ Note

The Seller asserts the lease notification obligation (DD-007) is not a consent requirement, and Mossvale's assignment restriction (DD-009) isn't triggered by a share sale. These *may* be correct for a share deal, but they are **the Seller's characterisations**, not confirmations. Verify the actual clause wording ourselves — change-of-control provisions frequently bite even on share sales.

---

# Summary of Recommendations

**Critical — revert to playbook, do not concede (no Frost authority given):**
1. Cap → **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (reject 20%).
2. Thresholds → de minimis **AUD 5,000**, basket **AUD 50,000**, **first-dollar** recovery (reject the deductible mechanic).
3. General time limit → **24 months** (reject 18 months and the "all Claims" sweeper).
4. **Separate fundamental/title regime** — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge (reject the "administrative simplicity" merger).
5. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — unwaivable.
6. **Delete buyer-knowledge bar** (Clause 8.3), especially the "discoverable" constructive-knowledge language; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnities.

**High:**
7. **Reject deemed/whole-data-room/public-register disclosure**; require specific, fair disclosure.
8. **Bluefen** — CP requiring effective consent **and** satisfied/evidenced conditions pre-Completion (not reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery).
9. **Riverlark** — payout statement + direct repayment from completion funds + effective security release; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking **and Frost approval**.
10. **Bonuses** — AUD 420,000 **plus on-costs** as explicit funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
11. **Title** — require independent verification; DD-012 register is not proof.

**Medium:**
12. **Ironquay** — broaden indemnity to IP-transfer consequences, preserve SOW3 cure; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
13. **DD-006 incident** — covenants to preserve logs, investigate, update; consider specific indemnity; stay neutral on breach/notification.
14. **Tax/IP** — reject "settled"; keep separate and open; no general-regime override.

**Lower / verify:**
15. **Sandbar renewals** — assess terminable/accrued status and "read-together" timing; no automatic Debt/price deduction.
16. **Lease/Mossvale** — independently verify the Seller's "no consent required" characterisations.

**Internal flags for the deal team:** Items 1, 3 and 9 (and any move to 20% cap / 18 months / post-completion Riverlark release) require **Amelia Frost's written authorisation identifying the draft** before we concede — none has been given. Note too that the Seller presents several of these as already-"negotiated"/"agreed" positions; they are not, and we should correct that framing in our mark-up.

Would you like me to draft the mark-up or a response letter putting these positions to the Seller?
